overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers for the file “Weights and Measures. Japan.” records a single item dated April 1, 1933, from Kobe and attributed to Donovan. The indexed item was a translation of a communication from the Japanese Woolen Goods Association announcing its adoption of the metric system for measuring cloth and requesting that American woolen-goods exporters be informed of the change; the underlying communication is not included on this page.

people.name: Donovan
people.role: Sender named in the index entry, apparently a U.S. official at Kobe; precise position is not stated

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on Japanese weights and measures
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes a translation concerning the Japanese Woolen Goods Association’s adoption of metric cloth measures and its request to notify American exporters.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State filing sheet contains one entry under “Weights and Measures. Japan.” It records an April 1, 1933 communication from Kobe, associated with Donovan, transmitting a translation of a notice from the Japanese Woolen Goods Association. The association had adopted the metric system for cloth measurements and wanted the change brought to the attention of American woolen-goods exporters.

interest: The sheet offers concise evidence of the international commercial consequences of Japan’s metrication, particularly for the textile trade. It is useful for tracing how Japanese trade associations used diplomatic channels to communicate technical standards to foreign exporters. As only an index survives here, it also identifies a potentially valuable underlying translation that may have been filed elsewhere or lost.
